correctness.rationale: The flag-support lemma is proved by minimal induced support and Mayer–Vietoris, including equality forcing the cross-polytope boundary. A Cayley quotient argument classifies exactly two 4-edge induced matchings in each of five directions, yielding ten and no smaller carriers. The standalone program enumerates all 392 simplices and 12870 eight-subsets and constructs exact signed boundaries. It checks B3 Z=B3 B4=0, rank mod 2 B3=95, all 25 nonzero Smith factors of [B4|Z] equal 1, B4 rank16, and the explicit integral relation B4 t+Z q=0. Since im[B4|Z] is a saturated rank25 sublattice of the rank25 kernel of B3, it equals the kernel integrally. The ten classes generate H3 with one primitive ±1 relation; no finite-to-infinite extrapolation is made.

value.rationale: Induced support and primitive integral generation are natural local-to-global invariants not determined by a known ambient wedge of nine 3-spheres. The theorem supplies a complete shortest-support classification for the canonical 16-vertex folded five-cube, a group-invariant affine hyperplane description, and an exact all-ten relation in which any nine form an integral basis. The combinatorial quotient argument explains why ten spheres, while the Smith lattice computation establishes meaningful integral rather than merely rational generation. The result does not rely on an arbitrary unmotivated parameter slice or on the already-known Betti number as its sole contribution.
